**Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F** is a localized healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] in Denmark. It functions as a key organizational unit in the national monitoring and quality improvement framework for the treatment of [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), as overseen by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP). 

The cluster is particularly significant in the 2024 RKKP quality reports for its performance on anticoagulation treatment metrics. Notably, Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F failed to meet the national quality standard of 90% for Indikator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 87.5% [^src1]. Additionally, the cluster recorded the lowest proportion among its peers for [[indikator-4a1|Indikator 4a1]] (1-year treatment coverage), scoring 85.1% (95% CI: 81.2–88.4) [^src2]. 

Beyond treatment coverage, the cluster's clinical outcomes are closely tracked across a variety of metrics to evaluate patient safety and long-term health. These include the incidence of ischemic stroke (apoplexy) measured under [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src4], as well as the rates of severe bleeding, heart failure, and mortality within one year of a new diagnosis [^src6] [^src7]. The data collected from Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F and other clusters is mapped geographically and analyzed hierarchically, enabling Danish health authorities to benchmark clinical practices, identify local variations in care, and drive targeted quality improvements in cardiovascular disease management.
